title: Hiring Screen: Senior Backend Engineer - Samir Khan
summary: Initial phone screen for Senior Backend Engineer. Candidate has 6 years experience, currently at TechNova, strong Go/Python background, worked on microservices and Kafka. Discussed remote flexibility, interview loop, and next steps (take-home + onsites). Recruiter to send interview schedule and compensation band.
next_steps: Ava to send interview loop details and compensation band via email (by 2025-04-01)
Candidate to confirm availability for take-home and onsite (within 3 business days)
Miguel to review candidate notes and decide on take-home assignment

Owner:Samir Khan | Item:Confirm availability for take-home + onsite | Due:2025-04-02

transcript:
Header: 2025-03-28 10:00 PT | Duration: 30m | Attendees: Ava Thompson, Miguel Santos, Samir Khan

[00:00] Ava Thompson: Hey Samir, thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood Inference, I'm the recruiter on the role, got Miguel the hiring manager with me, how are you today?
[00:08] Samir Khan: Hey Ava, thanks, doing well. Appreciate you all taking the time.
[00:12] Miguel Santos: Hi Samir, quick hi from me. Can you hear ok?
[00:15] Samir Khan: Yep loud and clear.

[00:30] Ava Thompson: Great, quick agenda: 20 minutes of background and role fit, 5 minutes logistics—notice, comp—then next steps. Sound good?
[00:35] Samir Khan: Yep that works.

[01:05] Miguel Santos: Can you give us a quick run of your recent experience at TechNova and what you worked on?
[01:15] Samir Khan: Sure. I've been at TechNova for about three years. I'm on the backend infra team, mostly Go, some Python. I own a microservice platform that manages event ingestion—Kafka pipelines, stream processors, and some near-realtime APIs. I did lots of work on reliability, partitioning, handling backpressure and reprocessing. Prior to that I was at Cloudily doing full-stack but focused more on services.
[02:10] Miguel Santos: Nice. When you say event ingestion, what's the scale? messages per second, retention?
[02:20] Samir Khan: Right now we peak around 25k msgs/sec across partition groups, retention is 7 days for hot tier, we move to cold storage after that. We shard by tenant and use a combination of compaction and TTL. We've tuned the producers for idempotency; had to deal with reordering a couple times.
[03:05] Miguel Santos: Any experience with LLMs or inference infra? Not required but curious.
[03:12] Samir Khan: Limited. I've integrated model inference calls—mostly calling external APIs and building batching proxies for throughput, but haven't run heavy GPU workloads or on-prem inference stacks.
[03:28] Ava Thompson: Totally fine. This role is heavily focused on backend infra and performance; we do expect familiarity with distributed systems patterns.

[04:00] Miguel Santos: Can you talk about a specific reliability incident you owned and how you addressed it?
[04:10] Samir Khan: Sure—one outage was related to a cascading failure when a downstream storage S3 endpoint got throttled. We saw producer retries pile up, consumers fell behind, and the service started OOMing due to retained buffers. I implemented circuit-breaker backpressure at the ingress, added adaptive batching, and introduced async spillover to a durable queue. We also added end-to-end tracing to see where latency spiked. After that we improved SLOs and added runbook steps.
[05:05] Miguel Santos: Nice, was there a measurable improvement?
[05:10] Samir Khan: Yes 99th latency dropped from ~1.2s to 450ms under load and incidents reduced by about 60% for that class.

[06:00] Ava Thompson: Can you share your primary languages and comfort level?
[06:05] Samir Khan: Go is primary, comfortable in Python, some Java earlier in career. I write tests, CI/CD pipelines, and use k8s for deployments.
[06:30] Miguel Santos: How about observability—Prometheus, Jaeger, logs?
[06:35] Samir Khan: Prometheus + Grafana for metrics, Jaeger for tracing, ELK stack for logs. We also built some internal dashboards for SLA alerts.

[07:10] Miguel Santos: What's your experience with databases—RDBMS, NoSQL?
[07:15] Samir Khan: Have used Postgres for transactional workloads, Cassandra for wide-column needs, and Redis for caching. Designed schema for high write throughput and eventually consistent access patterns.

[08:00] Ava Thompson: Shifting to logistics—what's your notice period and earliest start?
[08:05] Samir Khan: I have a two-week notice but would prefer four weeks to wrap up some projects.
[08:15] Ava Thompson: Ok that's reasonable. Compensation range expectations?
[08:20] Samir Khan: I'm targeting 180k-210k base depending on equity and remote flexibility.
[08:30] Miguel Santos: We're typically competitive; we'll share band ranges.

[09:00] Ava Thompson: Are you open to remote or do you prefer on-site?
[09:05] Samir Khan: Remote is preferred, open to occasional travel to SF for onboarding.

[10:00] Miguel Santos: Interview loop would be: take-home assignment, then two 1-hr technical onsites (system design + deep dive, and coding/design), and an interview with product/manager. Does that sound ok?
[10:15] Samir Khan: Sounds good. How long is the take-home intended to be?
[10:20] Miguel Santos: We aim for a 3-4 hour problem; we review for correctness and thinking.

[11:00] Ava Thompson: Any questions about team/org?
[11:05] Samir Khan: Curious about team size and cadence—how many backend engineers on infra?
[11:12] Miguel Santos: Right now infra is 8 engineers, small subteams around ingestion, routing, and storage. We do biweekly sprints and have a strong on-call rotation.

[12:00] Samir Khan: What's the expectation on on-call?
[12:05] Miguel Santos: Typically 1:6 rotation, mostly pager and escalation. We have good tooling to reduce toil.

[13:00] Ava Thompson: Quick technical question: how would you design a KV cache for low-latency lookups in front of a model-serving layer? Not full design, just thought process.
[13:12] Samir Khan: I'd consider an in-memory LRU with TTL, use consistent hashing for sharding, ensure cache invalidation hooks on writes, and maybe tier hot keys in fast memory. For persistence fallback, async write-through. Also consider batching to reduce request fanout to model servers and local hot-key replication to avoid cold starts.
[14:10] Miguel Santos: Good, follow-up: how to handle cold-start penalty when a model shard spins up?
[14:20] Samir Khan: Warmup requests, keep a small standby pool, and use a progressive ramp for traffic. Also cache shared artifacts and use KV of embeddings for quick checks.

[15:00] Miguel Santos: Any preference on languages for the role?
[15:05] Samir Khan: Go backend is ideal. I'm comfortable owning services in Go.

[16:00] Ava Thompson: Ok last section—do you have any questions about the recruiting process?
[16:05] Samir Khan: Just timeline—when would I hear back?
[16:10] Ava Thompson: We aim to get take-home out within 48 hours and have decisions on onsites within a week after submission. Final offers usually 2-3 weeks.

[17:00] Samir Khan: Sounds good. Also curious about equity and benefits briefly?
[17:10] Ava Thompson: We'll include compensation band and benefits summary in the email. Equity varies by level; we'll cover specifics if we move forward.

[18:00] Miguel Santos: Anything else tech-wise you want to add?
[18:05] Samir Khan: I have a repo of sample systems I've open-sourced; happy to share links if helpful.

[19:00] Ava Thompson: That would be great, please send links with your availability.

[20:00] Miguel Santos: Recap: Ava sends interview loop + comp band; Miguel prepares take-home rubric; Samir sends availability and repo links.

[20:15] Samir Khan: Got it. Thanks everyone.

[20:20] Ava Thompson: Thanks Samir, we'll follow up by email with next steps. Bye.

[20:25] Miguel Santos: Bye.

Note: minor transcription errors possible (names/PIDs). References: take-home rubric (internal doc), comp band (link to HR packet).
